clue.text: Go on about drink served with neck chop

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at tedious length
punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Someone nags about drink while serving a sharp blow to the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit punch is a short blow to the back of the neck, so a chop delivered there.

clue.text: Raised brass border

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A decorative edging made of raised brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns TUBA upwards in this down clue to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to border on something is to lie adjacent and touch it.

clue.text: Things that can bore coins

definitions.meaning: drill ... are the cutting parts that bore holes
small coins are called ..., as in a threepenny bit

explanation.definitionFit: Drill pieces that cut holes, and old slang for small change such as a threepenny piece.

clue.text: Hill workers being on time is a worry

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor
men are workers on a job

explanation.surface: Labourers on a hillside running late is a cause for concern.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to plague and harass them, a stronger form of fretting.

clue.text: America protects sailors vessels

indicators.note: protects means the first piece wraps around the second like a shield

parts.note: US is short for United States, i.e. America
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: The United States guards the boats of its naval men.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are vases or containers, and a vessel is any container for holding things.

clue.text: They duplicate work in rice production studies first

indicators.note: in places the work piece inside the reworked letters of rice
production suggests the letters of rice are made into something new

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word studies

explanation.surface: People researching how rice is grown, with work studies coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' makes CIER, which 'in' opens after its first letter; 'studies' is not a definition but supplies only its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Photocopiers are office machines that make duplicates of documents.

clue.text: A little backwards coming forward with information

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the phrase a little in reverse

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A shy person who comes forward with facts after holding back a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns A TAD round to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, the raw material of knowledge.

clue.text: Shift workers get transfer

parts.note: to shift is to change
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Shift workers are being moved to another post.
explanation.definitionFit: Property that changes hands passes from one owner to another, so is transferred.

clue.text: Disregarding dangers of skin infection

definitions.meaning: acting without regard to risk is reckless
a red eruption on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Reckless, heedless behaviour, and a patch of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: An urchin who's good, articulate and pines terribly

parts.note: to articulate words is to utter them

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of pines are badly messed up

explanation.surface: A well-behaved, well-spoken child who longs dreadfully for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a scruffy street child, so a ragged slum kid.

clue.text: Source of nutrient on salt lake

indicators.note: on places the next letter after the sailor in this across entry

parts.note: a tar or salt is old slang for a sailor

indicators.note: source of means the opening letter of the word nutrient

explanation.surface: Feeding a salt lake with something nourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is a sailor, TAR, not sodium chloride.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain pool in northern England.

clue.text: No surprise at finding the colossus isn't so!

definitions.meaning: the phrase is used to mean it is hardly surprising
the Colossus of Rhodes was one of the Seven Wonders, a huge one and far from tiny

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something unsurprising, and a playful description of a wonder of the world that is anything but tiny.

clue.text: Suffer fool changing places for attack

indicators.note: changing places says the two pieces swap round from the order the clue gives them

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to ail is to suffer from illness

explanation.surface: Putting up with an idiot who keeps moving around before an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing places' is the signal that the clue's own order of the two synonyms must be swapped before writing them in.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon someone violently or verbally.

clue.text: China accepts request for screening

indicators.note: accepts means the porcelain word takes the request inside it

parts.note: Ming is the fine porcelain of the Ming dynasty
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Beijing agrees to an application to show a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain: MING.
explanation.definitionFit: Masking is hiding or covering something from view, a form of concealment.

clue.text: Dresses at midnight before snow storm

parts.note: the middle of the word night is the letter G

indicators.note: storm suggests the letters of snow are whipped about

explanation.surface: Ball dresses worn at midnight before a blizzard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the centre letter of NIGHT; 'storm' reworks SNOW into OWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowns are long formal frocks.

clue.text: Variety available after a smoker's last fix

indicators.note: after puts the variety word behind the earlier pieces
last takes the final letter of the word smoker's

parts.note: a range is a variety, as of goods

explanation.surface: A selection on offer after someone has had their final cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available' simply goes with the range of goods on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a meeting is to organise or set it up.

clue.text: Up and about at a base

parts.note: the foot of something is its base

explanation.surface: Someone moving around at the bottom of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something afoot is in progress or astir.

clue.text: Sickness is a habit not applicable outside

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: NA is the form abbreviation for not applicable
use is custom or habit

explanation.surface: Being ill is a habit that does not apply when outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the form abbreviation round 'a habit'; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a queasy feeling of wanting to vomit.

clue.text: Posh people have time away before the first of September

indicators.note: before puts the earlier pieces ahead of the final letter

parts.note: off means away, as in going off

indicators.note: the first of takes the opening letter of September

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk take a holiday before autumn starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs is British slang for upper-class people.

clue.text: Bread and sugar

definitions.meaning: a sugarloaf is a moulded cone of sugar

explanation.definitionFit: A baked shape of bread, and a cone of refined sugar sold whole.

clue.text: Expressed gratitude, embracing a French swimmer

indicators.note: embracing means the thanks word holds the French article inside

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Someone said thanks while hugging a French swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a fish, and fish are swimmers.

clue.text: Bar that's popular with ghosts, oddly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of ghosts

explanation.surface: A pub that is a favourite haunt of spirits, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal such as gold.

clue.text: One short story on Scotsman's language

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short means the story word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
Ian is a typical Scottish name, standing for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A brief tale written in a Scottish man's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Off duty cab almost available!

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the cab word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
free means available

explanation.surface: A taxi with its light on, ready for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TAXI to TAX; 'Off duty' means without duty to pay, not off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods free of duty carry no tax.

clue.text: Everyone in the Tory left puts money into them

indicators.note: in places the everyone word inside the Tory group

parts.note: wets was Thatcher's term for moderate, left-leaning Conservatives
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Every left-wing Conservative invests money in something.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics WETS were the moderate Tories who opposed Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallets are purses for carrying banknotes, so cash is put into them.

clue.text: Rump parliament finally concocted denial

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of parliament
concocted suggests the letters of denial are cooked up anew

explanation.surface: The Rump Parliament eventually made up a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' reworks DENIAL into AILEND. The Rump Parliament was the purged English parliament of 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is the hindquarters, the back end.

clue.text: The old devil can, commonly

definitions.meaning: ... and can are both slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a nickname for Satan, and in British slang the nick is jail, as is the can.

clue.text: Men at work held up by power cut

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Workmen delayed by an electricity outage.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'held up' reads poWER Cut upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a team of workers.

clue.text: Rave about the woman

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of rave are moved around

explanation.surface: Enthusing over a particular lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's name.

clue.text: Giant who found source of gold in mineral

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the mineral word

parts.note: ore is a mineral that metal is mined from

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of gold

explanation.surface: A giant discovers where gold comes from in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous man-eating giant of folk tales.

clue.text: Opening financial analysis ignored union leader

indicators.note: ignored means a letter is left out of the audit word

parts.note: an audit is an inspection of accounts

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of union

explanation.surface: An initial review of accounts that a trade union boss overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' is a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is an entrance tunnel into a mine.

clue.text: Servicemen pumped up for action

parts.note: emergency-service crew who pump water at blazes, not keen soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: Firefighters are an emergency service who use pumps to put out blazes.

clue.text: Viewers' positive reaction on Spain

indicators.note: on places the reaction after the country letter in this across entry

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
yes is a positive response

explanation.surface: TV audiences react well to a programme about Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs we see with, so they are the lookers.

clue.text: Fights for bookings

explanation.definitionFit: Battles between forces, and appointments made in a diary.
